title: LEAP: Local ECT-Based Learnable Positional Encodings for Graphs
claim: A local structural encoding is computed through a clear four-stage sequence: select, normalize, transform, then project into a compact vector.
layout: 4 numbered panels in 2x2 grid, reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom, yellow arrows
description: A 2x2 grid of rounded cream panels numbered 1 to 4, linked by pale yellow block arrows. Panel 1 shows a graph with a red focal node and small colored feature squares beside the nodes. An arrow leads to the same graph with only the focal node's 1-hop neighborhood kept dark and the rest faded to gray. Panel 2 shows the neighborhood triangle placed off-center on coordinate axes. An arrow leads to the triangle rescaled and centered inside a unit circle. Panel 3 shows the neighborhood scanned along three directions, drawn as red, blue and magenta rotated frames with arrows. These feed a matrix of colored cells with rows θ and columns t. Panel 4 shows the matrix passing through a trapezoid labeled Projection into a short colored vector. This vector attaches to the focal node in the original graph. The eye goes first to the red node, then follows the arrows.
caption: Steps for computing the LEAP PE using 1-hop neighborhoods. (1) The neighborhood of a node in a featured graph is selected. (2) Normalization of the neighborhood features. (3) Computation of the differentiable ECT. (4) Projection of the matrix representation of the ECT to get the PE vector.
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) largely rely on the message-passing paradigm, where nodes iteratively aggregate information from their neighbors. Yet, standard message passing neural networks (MPNNs) face well-documented theoretical and practical limitations. Graph positional encoding (PE) has emerged as a promising direction to address these limitations. The Euler Characteristic Transform (ECT) is an efficiently computable geometric-topological invariant that characterizes shapes and graphs. In this work, we combine the differentiable approximation of the ECT (DECT) and its local variant ($\ell$-ECT) to propose LEAP, a new end-to-end trainable local structural PE for graphs. We evaluate our approach on multiple real-world datasets as well as on a synthetic task designed to test its ability to extract topological features. Our results underline the potential of LEAP-based encodings as a powerful component for graph representation learning pipelines.
